newsitem.title: BURMA: Indonesia sees Burma as prospective gas supplier.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees Burma as prospective gas supplier.

text.p: Indonesia is negotiating with Burma's military government over the prospect of buying natural gas from big offshore fields in the Bay of Mottama in southern Burma, Indonesian diplomats said on Monday.

The sources said any future Indonesian purchase of Burmese natural gas would come under the framework of a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on bilateral cooperation in the energy sector signed by the two countries in mid-October.

They said an Indonesian delegation arrived in Rangoon recently to negotiate with their Burmese counterparts following a visit in mid-October by Indonesian Oil Minister Sudjana and Faisal Abda'oe, the chief of state oil company Pertamina.
Burma is currently developing its Yadana and Yetagun offshore fields. It will pipe natural gas from the fields onshore in 1998, mostly for export to Thailand.
Burma's energy ministry estimated that the Yadana field in the Bay of Mottama contained about 5.7 trillion cubic feet of commercial reserves of natural gas.
Indonesian diplomats said the recently-signed MOU covered bilateral cooperation in both upstream and downstream energy sectors.
It includes technical and human resource assistance that Jakarta will provide to Burma in exploring new gas and petroleum resources and in modernising its run-down oil refineries.
They said Pertamina will likely send a few more delegations to Rangoon to negotiate with Burmese officials in 1997.
The sources did not exclude the possibility that Indonesia might supply Burma with crude oil and refined products in the future, saying it could come under bilateral talks.
